title: Accident Prevention Signs and Tags
summary: OSHA sets rules for danger signs, caution signs, safety instruction signs, traffic control signs, and accident prevention tags. Use the right one for the hazard and keep it visible.
talking_points: Signs and symbols must be visible at all times when work is being performed. Remove or cover them promptly when the hazard no longer exists.
Use danger signs only where an immediate hazard exists. They have a red upper panel, a black outline, and a white lower panel.
Use caution signs only to warn of potential hazards or unsafe practices. They are yellow, with a black panel and yellow "caution" lettering.
Safety instruction signs are white with a green upper panel and white letters. Directional signs are white with a black panel and a white symbol.
Exit signs, when required, use red letters at least 6 inches high on a white field.

At points of hazard, post construction areas with legible traffic control signs and protect them with traffic control devices. Signs, signals, markings, and barricades must follow Part 6 of the MUTCD.
Accident prevention tags are a temporary warning of a hazard such as defective tools or equipment. Never use a tag in place of a sign.
The ANSI standards named in the rule add more requirements. Follow them too.
site_hazards_to_check: Signs that are hidden, dirty, or damaged so they cannot be seen
Signs left up after the hazard is gone
Danger signs used for a potential hazard, or signs with the wrong colors
Defective tools or equipment with no accident prevention tag
Construction areas at points of hazard with no traffic control signs or devices
discussion_questions: What is the difference between a danger sign and a caution sign?
Which tools or equipment on this site need a tag right now?
Who checks that signs are visible and removed when the hazard is gone?

attribution.notice: Adapted from OSHA standard 29 CFR 1926.200, Accident prevention signs and tags. Reproduced with attribution for jobsite safety training; not an endorsement by OSHA.

flags: Verified against 29 CFR 1926.200(a)-(i) source text: colors, 6-inch exit lettering, MUTCD Part 6, tag rules and ANSI reference all match. Retitle fits content; 1926 citation correct.
Non-blocking: the talk does not reproduce ANSI Z535 specifications; crews must consult them for additional requirements (point 8 says so).
